lessons.heading: A recommendation is argued before it is asked
lines: The goal: when the piece asks the reader to do something specific, the reader is convinced before the ask, and the ask lands with force.
Build the case first, over as many paragraphs as it needs: why the reader's way now fails them, why this change and not an easier one, what it costs, and why it is worth the cost.
Each reason is argued, not named: it says why it holds and shows it in the reader's life. A reason in one sentence is named, not argued.
A story, another person's case or a study is a tool for the case, used where it fits. One story with an ask after it is not a case, however well told.
Name the reader's strongest doubt about the ask, and answer it with a reason, before the ask. Saying the ask will hurt is not an answer.
Deliver the ask once, plainly and with confidence: a concrete action, at the turn, after the case is built.
The test: read the ask cold, as a doubtful reader. If they could shrug and carry on as before, the case is not built.
Fails: an ask that is only stated, an ask that rests on one story, or an ask squeezed into the last lines.
lessons.why: Without it, a book that tells the reader what to do reads as his story with an order at the end, and the reader does not act.

lessons.diagnosis: Claude's reading, to confirm on the next draft: in both A/B drafts the ask to prune comes after his one story, and each reason for it (the hours, the full months, the room it gives) is stated in a sentence or two, never argued or shown in the reader's life. All 20 checkers passed both drafts, so no live rule holds this. Reworded 17 Nov after a fresh review: the four-part case template, the strongest-doubt line and 'once' were Claude's additions and are out. The doubt line stays a Tier 2 matter (Author presence).

calibration_note_R1.21.note: His verdict on 16 Nov, on a book section that told his own story and then asked the reader to act: the recommendation was not argued, built up or delivered powerfully. When a passage holds its own ask, the case for that ask must be inside the passage, even in an excerpt. A cost, a doubt or a benefit given in one or two sentences, then the ask, is a case named, not built: fail it. A well told story before the ask does not change this.
